sentences.text: Smoke from the grain elevator drifted across the studio shot all afternoon. You hear the squeal of steel tracks on asphalt long before the first hull crests the overpass. Tracer fire stitched the dark behind the correspondent, who never once broke off her sentence. Network producers will keep a live feed on the highway overnight, though the army says cameras must stay a kilometer back. Military police searched our van at the third roadblock, flipping through tapes, holding each cassette up to the light. Why would a family of five stand this close to a checkpoint that was shelled twice last night? Officials declined to confirm how many armored personnel carriers crossed the river, citing operational security, though our footage shows at least nineteen. So there we were, live on air, when the whole column just stopped — engines off, hatches open, crews smoking on the road. Analysts identified the vehicles as tracked self-propelled howitzers, most likely 2S19s, moving north in groups of three. A correspondent in a flak jacket knelt beside the guardrail, whispering her stand-up while the convoy idled behind her. Honestly, the weirdest part is the ice cream vendor still working the intersection while turrets swivel past him. Civilians lined the shoulder in silence; one old man raised two fingers at the passing armor, and nobody could say what he meant. By dawn the correspondents had relocated to a rooftop overlooking the bridge, where engineers were laying pontoon sections under sporadic fire. I counted the seconds between the flash on the ridge and the thud that rattled our satellite truck: eleven. How long can the checkpoint hold, our anchor asked, and the reporter on the ground simply shrugged into the lens. Her earpiece crackled with the producer's warning — mortars inbound — three seconds before the screen went to color bars. "They came through at three in the morning," the baker said, still in his apron, flour on his hands. At the edge of town, a boy on a bicycle races the lead vehicle for a hundred meters, then peels away laughing. "Back to you in the studio — we're hearing outgoing artillery again," Marisol shouted over the rotor noise. Tonight's broadcast opened with thermal footage of the convoy fording the shallows below the destroyed bridge. Chaperones counted heads twice before letting the fourth graders loose near the penguin colony. Somebody's lost mitten floated in the touch pool, right between two horseshoe crabs. Behind the gift-shop register, plush hammerheads outsold the stingray magnets three to one during spring break. Have you ever watched a giant Pacific octopus unscrew a jar to get at its herring breakfast? She had volunteered here eleven years and still paused, every shift, at the floor-to-ceiling window where the rays glided by. Gift-shop chatter faded as we entered the darkened jellyfish gallery, all hush and drifting light. What is the meaning of the word tank?
